subjects.meaningMnemonic: A tall box with a bar across the middle, like a window glowing with light. Picture the sun shining through it, so bright the glass seems split in two.
One flat line lying on its side. It is a single wooden plank laid across a muddy path so you can walk over it.
Three planks stacked and joined by one upright post, like the frame of a throne. Only a monarch gets to sit on something that sturdy.
A big empty square with nothing inside yet. It is a corral, a fenced pen waiting for animals to be herded in.
A tiny slanted dot, barely there. It is a speck of dust that landed on your page.
Two strokes leaning on each other like a pair of legs mid stride. This is a walker, always heading somewhere on foot.
One curved stroke sweeping down to the left. Hear the swoosh of a brush flicking across paper.
Two crossbars hung on a single post. Laundry gets draped over each bar, so this is a drying rack.
A bent little shape with a hand held out, hunched over and hoping. It is a beggar asking for spare change.
A figure with arms flung wide and legs spread apart. It looks just like a starfish lying flat on the sand.
One line across and one line down, crossing in the middle. It is a plus sign, the same one you use in maths.
Two flat lines, one above the other, the top one shorter. They are bunk beds, a small bunk stacked over a big one.
A trunk standing straight with branches above and roots spreading below. Someone shouts timber as it starts to fall.
A single straight line standing upright. It is a pole planted firmly in the ground.
A small square opening. It is a hatch in a ship's deck that you can pop open and climb through.
Many lines stream down from the top and flow out at the bottom. It is a head of long hair blowing in the wind.
Three points rise from one base, the middle one tallest. It is a ridge with three peaks against the sky.
A shape open at the top with walls on both sides. It is a bucket waiting to be filled.
A hand with a dot marking a spot on the wrist, the old way to measure a tiny length. That small measure is an inch.
A short line over a long line with a sprout pushing up between them. The long line is the ground, and the sprout grows out of rich soil.
Two halves facing each other with gaps between, like streets meeting from four sides. It is a crossroads in the middle of town.
This is only the left half of the crossroads, a narrow lane branching off. Call it a side street.
A big eye perched on top of two legs. It is a watcher who walks around and stares at everything.
A tall box with two bars inside, like an eye turned on its side. Picture a round eyeball rolling inside it.
Two long legs and nothing else, one bending out at the bottom. Someone is wobbling along on stilts.
A tall shape with a curved side and two bars inside. It is a thin crescent hanging in the night sky.
A slanted shape that seems to trail behind itself. It is someone walking slowly on dragging feet, in no hurry at all.
Two little loops twisted together. It is a tiny thread curled up after being pulled from a sweater.
A sharp blade on one side, ready to cut grain. It is a sickle swinging through a field.
Two short strokes point up and outward at the top. They are a pair of antlers poking out above a head.
Lines branch up from the soil like small leaves reaching for light. It is a seedling just breaking through.
A shape with an open frame like a raised palm. Slap it for a high five.
Two matching panels side by side with a gap between. They are saloon doors that swing open when you push through.
A straight stick with a short mark sticking off one side. It is a fortune stick shaken from a cup to tell your future.
A square split into four smaller squares. It is a paddy seen from above, divided into flooded plots.
The sun rises in the morning and sets at night. Everything that happens while the sun is up fills one whole day.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Each day you find a sunny niche by the window to sit in. Niche sounds like にち, the reading of day. It can also be read じつ in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: There is only one plank across the stream, so only one person can cross at a time. One plank means one.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Standing on that one plank, you get an itch on your back and cannot reach it without falling. Itch sounds like いち.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A monarch stands inside a corral with a speck of gold on the crown. Everything inside that fence belongs to the monarch, and that land is a country.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The whole country has one royal cook who feeds every citizen. Cook sounds like こく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The walker is always on the move. Every walker you pass on the street is a person.
subjects.readingMnemonic: That person is carrying a bottle of gin home after a long day. Gin sounds like じん. In some words it is read にん instead.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, a beggar pulls a plank off the drying rack and carves one notch in it. He adds a notch every time winter comes around, counting each year.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A kind nun gives the beggar a warm meal once a year. Nun sounds like ねん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: This starfish stretches its arms as wide as it can to look impressive. It wants you to see how large it is.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The large starfish took a bath in purple dye and now it glows. Dye sounds like だい. It can also be read たい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Write a plus sign and count its four arms, then count the ends and the middle twice for good luck. Somehow you always end up at ten.
subjects.readingMnemonic: You win ten shiny prizes, and every one is a jewel. Jewel sounds like じゅう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Bunk beds hold exactly two sleepers, one on top and one below. Bunk beds mean two.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Climbing to the top of the bunk beds, you bang your knee on the rail. Knee sounds like に.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Shout timber, and the tree falls onto a plank laid on the ground. The wood is pressed into paper and bound into a book.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A goose sees you reading that book and gives a loud honk. Honk sounds like ほん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A pole is pushed straight through the middle of a hatch. The pole is now in the hatch, right inside it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Stuck in the middle of the hatch, you chew on a sandwich while you wait. Chew sounds like ちゅう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Her long hair has not been cut in years and now reaches the floor. That hair is long.
subjects.readingMnemonic: She has to tie up all that long hair before she sits down to chow. Chow sounds like ちょう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A pole stands in a bucket at the foot of three peaks. Climb the pole, step over the peaks, and you exit the valley.
subjects.readingMnemonic: On your way to the exit, green shoots spring up wherever you step. Shoots sounds like しゅつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Put a plank under the bunk beds and you have three flat lines stacked up. Plank plus bunk beds makes three.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Three buckets of sand are piled on top of each other. Sand sounds like さん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: You push a stick an inch into the soil and watch its shadow move with the sun. The shadow tells you the time.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is time to leave, so you jump into your jeep. Jeep sounds like じ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: At the crossroads you can turn down any side street you like. Whichever way you choose, you keep going.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Before going out, you grab your coat from the hook. Coat sounds like こう. It is also read ぎょう in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The watcher has one giant eyeball and walks around on stilts to get a better view. All it does is see.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The watcher sees a dog sleeping in its kennel. Kennel sounds like けん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A thin crescent hangs in the sky and slowly grows full, then shrinks again. That cycle takes one month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Once a month you try to get a good photo of the crescent. Get sounds like げつ. It is also read がつ for the months of the year.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Down a side street, someone walks on dragging feet, trailing a tiny thread from their coat. They are always lagging behind.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A goat trots behind them, nibbling the thread. Goat sounds like ご. It is also read こう in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A deer with antlers stands on a plank, holding a sickle under the crescent. It wants to go first and steps in front.
subjects.readingMnemonic: The deer calmly meditates before stepping in front, completely zen. Zen sounds like ぜん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A seedling pushes up through the ground and opens its first leaves. It is the start of a new life.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Every new life deserves a chance to say hello. Say sounds like せい. It is also read しょう in some words.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A high five uses your whole hand. Count the fingers on that hand and you get five.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Five goats line up to give you a high five with their hooves. Goat sounds like ご.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The sun peeks through the gap between the saloon doors. That gap is an interval, the space between two things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Someone has wedged a can in the space between the doors to keep them open. Can sounds like かん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A fortune stick stands upright on a plank, pointing to the sky. It always points above.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A joker climbs up above everyone and juggles on the plank. Joker sounds like じょう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A pole of timber stands in the middle of the paddy, laid across with a plank. The sun rises right behind it every morning, because it faces east.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Facing east at dawn, you dip one toe into the cold paddy. Toe sounds like とう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Someone on stilts is trapped in a corral and pokes a stilt out of each corner. That makes four.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Four sheep wander into the corral to keep them company. Sheep sounds like し. It is also read よん and よ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: On its own, the kanji for day also means the sun itself, the thing that makes the day.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi ひ. Picture the sun so hot you shout "hee!" when it touches your skin.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The kanji for one plus the little つ ending is how you count one thing.
subjects.readingMnemonic: This uses the kun'yomi ひと plus つ. The つ ending is the native Japanese way of counting objects.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One plus day gives one day, or a whole day from morning to night.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kanji use their on'yomi: いち from one and にち from day, which you already know.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is just the number one.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi いち, the same itch you remember from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a country or a region.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi くに, not the cook reading. Picture the royal cook saying "coo, nee" as he looks over his country.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One plus person means one person, or being all alone.
subjects.readingMnemonic: This is an irregular reading: ひとり. Learn it as a whole word; it does not use いち or じん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a person, someone.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi ひと, the same ひと you saw in 一人.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One person, then one person again: each person, one by one.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is simply ひとり said twice: ひとりひとり.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a year, or a person's age in years.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi とし, not the nun reading. Picture the nun counting years on her toes, "toe, she" says.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A large person is a grown up, an adult.
subjects.readingMnemonic: This is an irregular reading, おとな. It does not use だい or じん; learn it as one word.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The kanji for large plus the い ending makes the adjective big.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi おお plus きい, so おおきい. Picture someone shouting "oh!" at something big.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Another way to say big, used right before a noun.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Same おお as 大きい, but it ends in きな instead of きい: おおきな.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Large turned into an adverb: very much, greatly.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi おお plus いに: おおいに.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Large in importance: something considerable or great.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Here the kanji uses its other on'yomi たい, plus した: たいした.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means large or great, often as a size label.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi だい, the purple dye from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Ten plus day gives ten days, or the tenth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: This is a special date reading: とおか. Ten is read とお here and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number ten.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi じゅう, the jewel from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Two plus the つ counting ending: two things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi ふた plus つ: ふたつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Two plus person: two people, a pair.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Like 一人, this is irregular: ふたり. Learn it together with ひとり.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Two plus day: two days, or the second day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: ふつか. It does not use に or にち.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number two.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi に, the knee from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Twenty plus day: twenty days, or the twentieth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special reading: はつか. Learn it as one word, because none of the usual readings appear.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Two tens make twenty; this word means twenty years old.
subjects.readingMnemonic: When it means twenty years old, it has its own reading: はたち. A big birthday gets a special word.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means a book.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi ほん, the honk from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The book's own person: the person in question, the one themselves.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: ほん plus にん, the second reading of person.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The sun's origin: the land where the sun rises, Japan.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Day becomes に and book stays ほん: にほん. The stronger form にっぽん doubles the sound.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the inside of something.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi なか. Picture the inside of a box so dark you say "nah, ka" and back away.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Inside, then inside again: quite deeply, so very or considerably.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is なか said twice: なかなか. The 々 mark repeats the kanji before it.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Inside the year: all year round.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi, with a sound change: ねん plus じゅう, so ねんじゅう. The ちゅう of inside picks up a voiced sound.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Inside the day: during the daytime.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: にち plus ちゅう, squeezed into にっちゅう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The kanji for long plus the い ending: the adjective long.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi なが plus い: ながい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Exit as a verb: to leave or to go out.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi で plus る: でる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To make something exit: to take it out or put it out.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi だ plus す: だす. Compare でる, where you go out yourself.

meanings.text: to go out (e.g. on an excursion or outing)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To exit the house on an outing: to go out.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It starts with the kun'yomi で, then かける: でかける.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Three plus day: three days, or the third day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: みっか. Three is read みっ and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Three plus the つ counting ending: three things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi みっ plus つ: みっつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number three.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi さん, the sand from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Time, then time again: from time to time, sometimes.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It is とき said twice, and the second one softens to どき: ときどき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One plus hour: one o'clock, or one moment in time.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: いち plus じ, the jeep from the kanji: いちじ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means time or a moment.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi とき, not the jeep reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Going as a verb: to go.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi い plus く: いく.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Going about a task: to perform or carry it out.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the longer kun'yomi おこな plus う: おこなう.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The going part of a trip: the way there.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi い plus き: いき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: See as a verb: to see or to watch.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus る: みる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To make someone see: to show.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus せる: みせる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To see something you were looking for: to find it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus つける: みつける.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To be seeable: to be visible or in sight.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus える: みえる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To get seen at last: to be found.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi み plus つかる: みつかる. Compare みつける, where you do the finding.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One plus month: a span of one month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi ひと plus つき: ひとつき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the Moon, or a month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi つき, not the get reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Years and months together: a long stretch of time.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both kun'yomi: とし plus つき: としつき.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Behind as a place: the back or the rear.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi うし plus ろ: うしろ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means after, or what comes behind.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi あと, not the goat reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the front, or before.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi まえ, not the zen reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Life arriving: to be born.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi う plus まれる: うまれる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Life as a verb: to live.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi い plus きる: いきる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To bring something to life: to produce or cause it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the on'yomi しょう plus じる: しょうじる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means life or living.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi せい, the say from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: One life: a whole lifetime.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi, squeezed: いち plus しょう becomes いっしょう.

meanings.text: born in (country, month, imperial era, zodiac year, etc.)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Your birth, or the place you were born.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi う plus まれ: うまれ, like 生まれる without the る.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: A person's life.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: じん plus せい, the gin and the say: じんせい.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Five plus the つ counting ending: five things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi いつ plus つ: いつつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number five.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi ご, the goat from the kanji.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Five plus day: five days, or the fifth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: いつか. Five is read いつ and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The interval of time: time, an hour, a period.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: じ plus かん, the jeep and the can: じかん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means the space between things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi あいだ, not the can reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The one between people: a human being.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: にん plus けん, and けん softens to げん: にんげん.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: The span of a year: during a year.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Both on'yomi: ねん plus かん, the nun and the can: ねんかん.

meanings.text: to move something (to a higher place)

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To move something above: to raise it.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi あ plus げる: あげる.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means above or on top.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi うえ, not the joker reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: To go above: to rise or go up.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Here it uses the kun'yomi あ plus がる, so あがる, like あげる but going up by itself.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji means east.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it uses the kun'yomi ひがし, not the toe reading.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Four plus day: four days, or the fourth day of the month.
subjects.readingMnemonic: A special date reading: よっか. Four is read よっ and day is read か.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Four plus the つ counting ending: four things.
subjects.readingMnemonic: It uses the kun'yomi よっ plus つ: よっつ.

subjects.meaningMnemonic: Alone, the kanji is the number four.
subjects.readingMnemonic: Alone it keeps the on'yomi し, the sheep from the kanji. People also say よん.
